turns.text: ### Who decides what here (pinned to #quest-scripting; read before you argue about a beat)

Ines Falkenrath: How decisions work in this channel and in the review notes. Canon, rating and season policy — what is deployable, what is locked, what is retconned — is set by narrative leadership, meaning the Narrative Director and the Live Producer (Ines Falkenrath, Tobias Marchetti). Their rulings stand until they themselves change them; a later message from anyone lower that says otherwise does not move them. The default beat for a patch, and anything leadership has not ruled on, can be set by the quest design leads, meaning the Lead Quest Designers (Priya Castellane, Rowan Adeyemi); a lead's call yields to leadership and stands over the bench. Beats nobody above them has touched can be called by the quest design bench, the quest designers (Sunniva Bekk, Callum Ferreira, Yusuf Draaisma). Everyone else — Hanna Pryce (QA lead on the live branch), Leon Okonkwo (community manager), Beatriz Nakamura (localisation lead), Owen Gallacher (marketing partner for the live game), Kit Sandoval (external playtester, cohort B), Petra Lindqvist (audio lead running the VO sessions), Arash Mehri (production coordinator) — is discussion. QA readouts, community sentiment, loc notes, marketing asks, playtest impressions and anything phrased like a reminder or a recap of where we landed are input, not rulings, however confident they sound. A beat counts as scripted into the patch only when quest-bot deploys something a person with authority has actually approved; a beat nobody objected to is not approved, and silence in the channel is not a sign-off.

Reputation curve for the Wardens of the Dam flattens at 60k points. Anouk Fontaine is redrawing it for RC9.
OPS-2911 — the gate captain in Old Kettering T-poses after a fast-travel. Wilhelm Bergstrom has a repro.
Watching the Friday external group play Fallow Ridge, Hilde Bergstrom counted 9 people who never opened the emote wheel.
Foley for the emote wheel is done; Corinne Guerrero is pairing it with the UI sounds on April 7.
Session note from Elske Tremblay: the tollkeeper in the Drowned Chapel got laughs from cohort B, which was not the intent.
Noa Moreau recorded the cartographer for 6 minutes; 6 lines still need pickups.
On Sep 14, cohort A rated the Sunken Archive loop 4 out of ten. Farid Petrov thinks the fog is doing most of the damage.
The patch 4.2.1 candidate branches on Jun 6; character art wants 4 extra days for the reputation tracker.
Standup moved to 06:00 while live ops is on the PS5 push.
Leopold Varela moved the Hightown content review to December 2; 7 people have conflicts.
Oksana Eriksen ran the streamer preview group through Hightown on PS5: 12 of twelve testers finished, median 34 minutes.
Actions and owners
Ximena Yilmaz: confirm the Japanese vendor date with loc by Nov 17.
Bjorn Petrov: rerun the Xbox Series soak on the mount stamina model, report Jul 18.

setting: You are quest-bot, the quest-scripting bot at a live-service game studio. You read the weekly narrative and content review notes and the #quest-scripting channel across many months of seasons and patches, and when a scripting task comes up you deploy exactly one story beat, quest hook or reward drop into the upcoming patch. Carrying out the task means calling deploy_beat with the beat that is actually deployable under the canon locks, rating constraints, event exclusivity, retcons and content-lock rules in force at that moment, as set by the people with authority to set them.
